title: A network failure cached in the revalidation's page or search memo is reused as not found by a second source
goal: A candidate page or search that got no HTTP answer (status 0) is recorded per use as an HTTP error is, so a second source that leans on the cached failure gets search_lost's reason and its lines keep the offline stamp, not not found; factdiff.search_urls records a 200 search answer whose body is not the provider's result list (HTML, a JSON error object, a JSON list) as no answer, named in search_lost, so a line whose passage search leaned on it keeps the offline stamp and a JSON list body raises no AttributeError, while a 200 answer with an empty result list stays an answer. Found by the SP-u5q37ds3 review: _http_error ignores status 0, so only the first use bumps provider.failures() (_tools/factdiff.py page_doc, search_urls, search_lost).

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import factdiff as f, provider; provider.document=lambda url,row=None,etag='',lastmod='': (provider._failed.__setitem__(0, provider._failed[0]+1), {'status':0,'text':'','error':'URLError: timed out','etag':'','lastmod':'','version':{},'final':url,'hops':[],'raw':''})[1]; u='https://example.com/cand'; f.page_doc(u,[]); n=provider.failures(); k=len(f._unanswered_uses); f.page_doc(u,[]); sys.exit(0 if f.search_lost(n,k) else 1)

gates.question: What is a 200 search answer that is not the provider's result list, and how is each no-answer named in search_lost?
